findings.paper_title: Schools Balances and Medium-Term Financial Plans
findings.headline: School financial improvements in 2025/26 relied on one-off grants (£270k) and non-recurring income (£1.1m) unlikely to repeat
findings.detail: Schools projected a deficit of £889k for 2025/26 but closed with a £511k surplus. However, £1.1 million of this £1.4 million improvement came from non-recurring sources including Welsh Government year-end grants, ALN funding, secondment income and fundraising. The document explicitly states these sources cannot be relied upon for future budgets.
findings.matters: The improved 2025/26 outturn masks underlying budget deterioration. If one-off income does not repeat, the projected 2026/27 deficit of £1.23 million becomes more likely. Lenders and finance directors must distinguish between sustainable and temporary improvements.
findings.figures: 2025/26 improvement: £1.4m; attributed to £270k WG grants + £1.1m non-recurring income; 2026/27 projection: -£1.23m deficit
findings.quote: Many of the factors contributing to the improved 2025/26 outturn position are non-recurring and cannot be relied upon to support school budgets on an ongoing basis.

findings.paper_title: Schools Balances and Medium-Term Financial Plans
findings.headline: Schools report staffing cuts have reached breaking point and further reductions are not sustainable
findings.detail: Net 41 posts removed in 2026/27 to date (25 teaching, 5 support). Since September 2023, cumulative staffing reductions have been substantial. School leaders report that further sustainable workforce reductions are becoming increasingly limited. One school initiated a compulsory redundancy process.
findings.matters: When schools cannot cut staffing further without harming provision, options narrow: either accept educational decline or require council/government intervention. Limited maneuverability increases risk of unplanned deficit or service failure.
findings.figures: 2026/27 net staff reductions to date: 41 posts (approximately 25 teaching); cumulative reduction since Sept 2023 substantial
findings.quote: Many schools report that staffing levels have already been reduced substantially and that opportunities for further sustainable workforce reductions are becoming increasingly limited.

findings.paper_title: Schools Balances and Medium-Term Financial Plans
findings.headline: Primary sector pupil numbers declining 15% over five years, automatically reducing school funding
findings.detail: Actual primary pupils fell from 5,129 in 2024/25 to 4,908 in 2025/26 (221 pupils lost). Projections show further decline to 4,745 by 2026/27 and 4,383 by 2028/29. Since school funding is pupil-led (>70% of budgets), this automatic reduction compounds pressures. Schools cannot cut staffing proportionally in the short term.
findings.matters: Demographic decline is structural and irreversible. Automatic funding reduction forces either shrinking provision or unsustainable savings. This affects both school viability and local economic prospects.
findings.figures: Primary pupils: 5,129 (2024/25) → 4,908 (2025/26) → projected 4,383 (2028/29) = 15% decline over five years
findings.quote: Actual pupil numbers in the primary sector reduced from 5,129 in 2024/25 to 4,908 in 2025/26, a reduction of 221 pupils, and are projected to reduce further to 4,745 by 2026/27 and 4,383 by 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: Schools Balances and Medium-Term Financial Plans
findings.headline: School funding remains permanently 6.06% below prior baseline due to embedded cuts from 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.detail: Despite a better-than-expected Local Government Settlement in 2025 and no new cuts for 2026/27, the previous budget reductions remain baked into all school budgets as a permanent structural gap. This will not reverse absent external intervention.
findings.matters: This is not temporary cyclical pressure but a permanent structural reduction in the funding baseline. All schools operate under a lasting constraint, making budget balance increasingly difficult without fundamental change.
findings.figures: Embedded reduction: 6.06% for 2026/27 (compared to 6.33% in prior year)
findings.quote: However, the reductions applied in 2023/24 and 2024/25 remained embedded within school budgets, resulting in 2026/27 funding levels remaining 6.06% below those that would otherwise have been available.

findings.paper_title: Schools Balances and Medium-Term Financial Plans
findings.headline: Six schools now operating under Planned Licensed Deficits with recovery plans required
findings.detail: Two additional schools entered PLD status for 2026/27, bringing the total to six (up from four in the prior year). Each has submitted a formal recovery plan. Any failure of these plans would require escalated council intervention.
findings.matters: Multiple schools in formal deficit recovery plans indicates acute financial stress. If these plans fail, the council must either bail out schools or permit unplanned deficits, creating governance and financial risks.
findings.figures: 6 schools in PLD for 2026/27 (25% of estate); 2 newly entering, 4 continuing from 2025/26
findings.quote: Following these continued budget pressures, two additional schools have required a Planned Licensed Deficit (PLD) for 2026/27, bringing the total number of schools operating under a PLD to six, with four continuing from 2025/26.
